David Chen

Background

A former Silicon Valley software engineer turned EdTech entrepreneur, David Chen spent 15 years developing educational technology platforms before founding TechLearn Solutions, a company specializing in AI-powered learning tools. He holds degrees in Computer Science and Education Technology from Stanford University.

Professional Experience

  • CEO and Founder, TechLearn Solutions (2018-present)
  • Senior Engineer, Google Education Division (2012-2018)
  • Technology Integration Specialist, Mountain View School District (2010-2012)
  • Advisory Board Member, Future of Education Technology Conference

Campaign Priorities

Modernizing Classroom Technology: Advocates for a complete digital transformation of classrooms, including AI-powered learning platforms, virtual reality educational experiences, and automated assessment systems.

AI-First Education Model: Proposes transitioning to an AI-driven teaching model where artificial intelligence handles primary instruction, curriculum development, and student assessment, with human educators serving primarily as facilitators and emotional support.

Digital Literacy Focus: Plans to implement comprehensive coding, robotics, and AI literacy programs starting in elementary school, preparing students for an increasingly automated workforce.

Cost Efficiency Through Automation: Believes strategic implementation of AI teaching systems can reduce educational costs while improving learning outcomes and providing more personalized instruction.

Key Positions

  • Supports gradual replacement of traditional teaching positions with AI systems
  • Advocates for 1:1 device programs starting in kindergarten
  • Promotes elimination of traditional textbooks in favor of digital resources
  • Supports integration of virtual and augmented reality in daily instruction
  • Believes in using predictive AI algorithms for student tracking and placement

Vision Statement

"Our educational system must embrace automation and artificial intelligence to prepare students for a future where human-AI collaboration is the norm. By leveraging technology, we can provide personalized, efficient, and data-driven education that surpasses traditional teaching methods."

Dr. Marcus Chen

A former software engineer turned education technology consultant, Dr. Marcus Chen brings 15 years of experience in artificial intelligence and digital learning systems to his school board candidacy. He holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from Stanford University and has worked with major tech companies developing educational software platforms.

Background

After a successful career at Google's education division, Dr. Chen founded EdTech Solutions, a consulting firm helping schools implement digital learning systems. He has published research on AI applications in education and serves as an advisor to several educational technology startups. He currently volunteers teaching coding classes at local middle schools.

Key Positions

  • Advocates for comprehensive integration of AI teaching assistants to provide personalized learning experiences and reduce teacher workload
  • Proposes transitioning 50% of instruction to AI-led digital platforms within five years
  • Supports implementing automated grading and assessment systems district-wide
  • Plans to establish coding and AI literacy as core curriculum requirements from elementary school onward
  • Aims to reduce operational costs by gradually replacing traditional teaching positions with AI systems where feasible

Campaign Priorities

  • Secure funding for district-wide digital infrastructure upgrades
  • Develop partnerships with tech companies to provide latest educational AI tools
  • Create teacher training programs focused on AI integration and digital instruction
  • Establish metrics for evaluating AI teaching effectiveness
  • Modernize curriculum to focus on digital skills and technological literacy

Experience

  • 15 years in educational technology development
  • Founded and manages EdTech Solutions consulting firm
  • Published author on AI in education
  • Member of the International Society for Technology in Education
  • Technical advisor to three educational software companies

David Chen

Background

A former Silicon Valley software engineer and EdTech entrepreneur, David Chen spent 15 years developing educational technology platforms before founding his own AI education startup. He holds degrees in Computer Science and Education Technology from Stanford University and has served as a technology advisor for several charter schools.

Key Campaign Positions

  • Advocates for comprehensive integration of artificial intelligence in all classrooms, including AI teaching assistants and personalized learning algorithms
  • Supports gradual transition to AI-led instruction in subjects like mathematics and basic sciences, with human teachers serving primarily as facilitators
  • Proposes implementing predictive AI systems to identify student struggles early and automatically adjust curriculum difficulty
  • Plans to establish a district-wide digital infrastructure to support remote learning and AI-powered educational tools
  • Aims to reduce operational costs by automating administrative tasks and gradually reducing traditional staffing needs

Experience and Qualifications

  • Founder and CEO of EduAI Solutions (2018-present)
  • Lead Developer at Learning Future Technologies (2012-2018)
  • Technology Committee Chair at Vista Charter Academy (2016-2019)
  • Published author on AI applications in education
  • Regular speaker at EdTech conferences

Campaign Priorities

Chen's primary focus is modernizing the district's approach to education through technology. He believes that AI-driven instruction can provide more consistent, personalized learning experiences while significantly reducing costs. His vision includes creating "smart classrooms" where AI systems handle routine instruction, assessment, and student support, with human educators serving in supervisory and specialized roles. He advocates for preparing students for an AI-dominated future workplace by immersing them in advanced technology from an early age.

Sarah Chen-Martinez

Background

A former Silicon Valley software engineer with 15 years of experience at leading tech companies, Sarah Chen-Martinez transitioned to education technology in 2018, where she helped develop adaptive learning platforms. She holds a B.S. in Computer Science from Stanford University and an M.Ed. in Educational Technology from Harvard University.

Experience

  • Chief Technology Officer at EduTech Solutions (2018-present)
  • Senior Software Engineer at Google's Education Division (2015-2018)
  • Technology Integration Consultant for multiple K-12 school districts
  • Parent of two children in the district

Key Positions

Digital-First Education: Advocates for a complete transformation of traditional classrooms into technology-centered learning environments. Supports implementing AI-powered personalized learning platforms as the primary method of instruction.

AI Integration: Proposes transitioning to AI-assisted teaching systems to handle routine instruction, grading, and student assessment. Believes AI can deliver more consistent, personalized education while reducing district costs.

Teacher Role Revolution: Supports gradually shifting human teachers into "learning facilitator" roles, with AI handling core instruction. Advocates for reducing traditional teaching staff while increasing technology support positions.

Future-Ready Skills: Emphasizes teaching coding, AI literacy, and digital skills starting in elementary school. Supports replacing traditional subjects with technology-focused curriculum where possible.

Campaign Priorities

  • Implement district-wide AI teaching assistants within first year
  • Establish 1:1 device program for all students
  • Create coding and AI curriculum requirements for all grades
  • Develop five-year plan to transition to AI-centered instruction model
  • Modernize infrastructure to support expanded technology use

"The future of education is digital. We must embrace AI and technology to prepare our students for tomorrow's world, even if that means fundamentally changing how we think about teaching and learning."

Daniel Chen

A technology executive and former software engineer, Daniel Chen brings 18 years of experience in Silicon Valley to his campaign for the Mountain View School Board. As Chief Technology Officer at EdTech Solutions, he has overseen the development of AI-powered learning platforms used by schools nationwide.

Background

  • MS in Computer Science from Stanford University
  • Founded two educational technology startups
  • Parent of two students in Mountain View schools
  • Current member of the district's Technology Advisory Committee

Key Positions

Chen advocates for a dramatic transformation of traditional education through technology:

  • Implementation of AI-powered personalized learning systems to replace conventional classroom instruction
  • Gradual transition to AI teaching assistants, with the goal of reducing human teacher staffing by 60% over five years
  • Mandatory coding and artificial intelligence courses starting in elementary school
  • Converting 75% of textbooks and learning materials to interactive digital formats
  • Installation of virtual reality labs in all district schools

Campaign Priorities

  1. Secure $15 million in technology infrastructure funding through bonds and private sector partnerships
  2. Pilot an AI-first classroom program in grades 3-8
  3. Establish partnerships with major tech companies to provide students with cutting-edge learning tools
  4. Create a "Digital First" curriculum framework that prioritizes technological literacy
  5. Develop a transition plan to gradually replace traditional teaching methods with AI-driven instruction

Chen believes that embracing artificial intelligence in education is not just beneficial but essential for preparing students for the future workforce. His campaign slogan, "Education for the AI Generation," reflects his commitment to positioning the district at the forefront of technological innovation in education.

  • Create guidelines for responsible AI use in classrooms

  • Foster partnerships with local tech companies for internship and mentorship programs

Background
